summary.headline: R R Kabel Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33.7% YoY to INR2,964.1 crore, with EBITDA up 34.6% to INR263.5 crore and record full-year revenue of INR9,722.4 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with wires and cables (W&C) driving growth across domestic and export markets despite Middle East disruption and volatile copper, aluminium and PVC prices. FMEG revenue grew 13.8% YoY but breakeven slipped from March 2026 to FY27. Management flagged near-term export pressure in Q1 FY27 from the Middle East conflict, with April described as normal outside that region. A dividend of INR5.50 per share was declared, taking FY26 dividend to INR9.50 per share.

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR2,666.4 crore (+36.3% YoY) and FY26 revenue INR8,763.7 crore (90% of group revenue); segment profit INR257.3 crore in Q4 and INR775.6 crore for FY26. Q4 volume growth about 10%: wires single-to-mid single digit, cables high teens.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR297.7 crore (+13.8% YoY) and FY26 revenue INR958.6 crore (+3%, about 10% of group revenue). Losses narrowed YoY; breakeven now targeted for FY27 versus March 2026 earlier, due to weak weather-driven volumes and slow pass-through of input costs.

guidance_outlook: W&C volume growth guided at 16-18% a year, above industry growth; management said FY27 W&C volume growth of 16-18% remains the target.
Project RRise targets: W&C EBIT margin 10.5% by FY28 (about 130 bps achieved so far versus 300 bps planned), 18% W&C CAGR, 25% FMEG CAGR, 2.5x EBITDA over three years.
FY27 group EBITDA margin guided at 9.5%, per an analyst's reading of management's response.
FMEG value growth target of 20-25% in FY27; breakeven now targeted in FY27.
Management indicated that, with 16-18% volume growth and pricing, FY27 top-line growth of about 30% is mathematically plausible; no formal revenue guidance given.
Wire volume growth expected around 11-12% and cable around 25% over the next two years; cable share of W&C mix could rise by 3-4 percentage points to about 31% by year-end.
Q1 FY27 export impact expected to be larger than Q4 given the Middle East conflict; Middle East about 12% of group revenue (about 40% of W&C exports, which are about 30% of W&C).
capex_capacity: INR1,200 crore capex programme for FY26-FY28; about INR300 crore spent in FY26; majority of the balance to be spent in FY27.
Current cable capability up to 66 kV; the expanded programme targets up to 220 kV (lower end of EHV / higher end of HV).
Capacity additions planned every six months; some capacity to come in mid-FY27 and by end-FY27, with full completion by FY28.
Cable capacity utilisation already above 90%, driving the need for new cable capacity.
Expansion focused on cable and wire capacity plus operating efficiencies, aimed at faster cable order execution.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as healthy and normal through March and April; management reported no major channel destocking.
Export strong in Q4, with export volumes above domestic; exports about 30% of W&C, of which about 40% go to the Middle East.
Pricing is passed through on a continuous basis; a price change is made when raw material prices move 2-3%, using a 15-20 day average. One price increase taken in April.
Management said cumulative price rises since the start of FY26 have been more than double-digit.
Product mix about 73% wire and 27% cable in FY26 (copper price rise inflated the wire share in revenue).
Data centre opportunity identified, but management said it is not yet a substantial part of revenue; supplies through direct and distribution channels.
Inventory up (about 8 days higher inventory days) on in-transit exports and higher metal prices; payables rose on greater use of letters of credit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise sharply, and what drove the payables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed higher inventory to in-transit export shipments and metal prices up about 20-30%; it said the impact was about 8 days. Payables rose because the company used letter of credit facilities more actively.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an inventory gain in Q4 and how large is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was a marginal positive inventory impact in Q4 as part of normal business, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East export impact be larger in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said Q1 is likely to see more impact than Q4 because March disruption persisted into April, with duration of the conflict the key variable; it expects other geographies to compensate in part.

qa_highlights.question: How much of cable and wire could be sold at peak capacity, and is there a risk of oversupply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a peak revenue or rupee guidance, citing raw material and mix variability. It sees no oversupply risk for itself given its B2B expansion and demand outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin expansion achievable in FY27 given copper prices and new competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 9.5% margin target for FY27 and the 10.5% W&C EBIT margin by FY28 target, based on volume growth, mix, utilisation and scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 revenue given volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal rupee guidance; management said mathematically volume growth plus price rise could yield about 30% growth in FY27 on average.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict disrupting exports (about 12% of group revenue) and likely to weigh more heavily in Q1 FY27.
Copper, aluminium and PVC volatility, and pass-through lag, particularly in FMEG.
Rising inventory days and receivables/payables dynamics, including reliance on letters of credit.
FMEG breakeven slipping to FY27; weather-driven demand and competitive pressure in the second half.
Capacity additions over six-month intervals and execution of the INR1,200 crore capex plan; cable capacity utilisation above 90%.
Management's margin targets (9.5% FY27 group margin; 10.5% W&C EBIT margin by FY28) depend on sustained pricing and mix; a non-quantified inventory gain helped Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume growth and Project RRise targets, but cautious on the Middle East export outlook and FMEG profitability, which slipped. Management avoided quantifying the Q4 inventory gain, peak capacity revenue and rupee guidance.
key_quotes: We delivered our highest ever quarterly and annual revenue, supported by steady demand and disciplined execution across the business.
Importantly, FMEG losses have reduced as compared to last year, and we remain on track to achieve breakeven in FY27.
Like, we used a letter of credit facility , so that we can, e effectively manage our working capital.
Since in cable already we are at optimum utilization of more than 90% so to meet this growth plan we will keep adding capacity.

adds.what: Cable capability expansion from 66 kV up to 220 kV under INR1,200 crore FY26-FY28 capex programme

growth.why: Management guides W&C volume growth of 16-18% for FY27 and says ~30% top-line growth is mathematically plausible (no formal revenue guidance), backed by a INR1,200 crore capex programme (cable to 220 kV, ~INR300 crore spent in FY26, majority in FY27) with cable utilisation above 90%, though Q1 FY27 export pressure from the Middle East is flagged.
